page.title: Release readiness
page.purpose: Walk the owner through Apple's path — the most opaque part of shipping an iOS app — naming at every rung what is done, what is blocked, and what only a person can do.

priorities.statement: Rungs are ordered, and a later rung never reports ready while an earlier one is not.
priorities.notes: Certificates cannot be ready while enrollment is not. Order is the information.

priorities.statement: Each rung states plainly whether the ramp can complete it or only the owner can.
priorities.notes: Enrollment, identity verification, 2FA, and payment are irreducibly human. Implying automation that cannot exist wastes the owner's time.

priorities.statement: The enrollment rung shows its recurring cost, not just a status.
priorities.notes: $99/yr is a decision. A rung that reads only 'not started' hides that it is a purchase.

priorities.statement: The build-host rung reports both whether it can validate and whether it can produce submittable builds.
priorities.notes: These diverge on an Intel host, and the divergence is dated and foreseeable rather than a surprise.

priorities.statement: Rung state is re-probed, never read from a stored flag.
priorities.notes: A lapsed membership must not continue to read as satisfied.

states.description: No Apple Developer Program enrollment. The first rung is the only actionable one; every later rung is explicitly blocked by it. The mirror path is surfaced as the one thing that works without it.
Enrollment submitted but not granted. Distinguishes 'waiting on Apple' from 'waiting on you'.
Every rung satisfied, but the fulfilling build host will stop producing submittable builds when the SDK floor next rises. Shown as a dated warning, not a failure.
Every rung satisfied; TestFlight upload is available.

claims.statement: No rung reports ready while any rung it depends on is unsatisfied.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-009. A ladder that reports a later rung ready out of order is displaying independent flags, not modelling a dependency.

claims.statement: Every rung indicates whether it can be automated by the ramp or requires an owner action.
claims.rationale: The purpose of the surface is to tell the owner what to do next; conflating 'blocked on you' with 'blocked on the system' defeats it.

claims.statement: When enrollment is absent, the surface names the physical-device path that needs no enrollment, and states that its evidence cannot gate a release.
claims.rationale: S2I-P1-003. Without this the owner concludes that no physical-device work is possible at all, which is false — but presenting it without the non-promotable caveat would be misleading in the other direction.

claims.statement: A build host approaching or past its submittable-build capability shows the specific requirement it will fail, not a generic warning.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-004. 'This host may stop working' is not actionable; 'Xcode 27 requires Apple Silicon' is.
